key_insight: GUILD proposes guiding robot demonstration collection iteratively, rather than relying solely on teleoperator intuition or filtering data afterward. The goal is to collect more useful training data from the start.
problem_solved: Real-world teleoperation is expensive, and unguided demonstrations may contribute little to policy performance. Post-collection filtering can improve datasets but cannot recover the effort spent collecting low-value data.
method: Use guided, iterative data collection for imitation learning, as indicated by the paper’s title.
Focus on improving which demonstrations are collected, rather than only curating an existing dataset.
The supplied abstract is truncated; specific guidance mechanisms, iteration steps, and evaluation results are unavailable.
impact: Better-targeted demonstrations could reduce wasted teleoperation effort and make robot policy training more data-efficient. Quantitative benefits cannot be assessed from the provided excerpt.
